prompt: Given an unweighted directed graph (adjacency dict) and a start node, return a dict mapping every reachable node to its minimum number of hops from start (start itself is 0). Unreachable nodes are left out.
hint: You need the distance to every node, not one target. Which traversal reaches nodes in order of distance from the start?

recognize.text: Says distance grows by one for each level of the traversal

explain.text: Explains that a node's distance is its parent's distance plus one, set the first time it is discovered
Explains that a visited/distance map stops cycles from looping forever

variant.prompt: Twist: instead of every distance, return the sorted list of nodes that are exactly k hops from start.

followUp: Explain how your code makes sure each node's distance is the smallest one, and what stops it looping on a cycle.
